newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia sees 1997 budget proposal by August.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia sees 1997 budget proposal by August.

text.p: Slovenia's deputy prime minister Marjan Podobnik said on Thursday he expected the government to finalise a budget proposal for 1997 and send it to parliament by the end of next week.

"The (coalition) parties are determined to adopt and pass the budget proposal to parliament (by August 1)," Podobnik told a news conference, but said it was unlikely the government would pass the proposal at its Thursday session.
The opposition has called for a parliamentary debate on the government's effectiveness, mainly as a result of its failure to draw up a budget proposal for 1997.
The government blames the delay on the fact that the coalition was only formed at the end of February after inconclusive elections in November last year.
Podobnik's conservative People's Party rules in coalition with the dominant centre-left Liberal Democrats and the pensioners' party Desus.

Podobnik reiterated earlier forecasts that government spending in 1997 should not exceed 730 billion tolars ($4.4 billion) while the budget deficit should reach up to one percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
In 1996 GDP was 1,181.2 billion tolars, while government spending amounted to 597.5 bilion tolars on income of 613.8 billion.
